newsitem.title: DENMARK: Deaths feared in Danish biker gang war blast.
newsitem.headline: Deaths feared in Danish biker gang war blast.

text.p: A blast hit the Hell's Angels gang's central Copenhagen base on Sunday and there were fears that it had caused deaths and injured a number of people in what appeared to be another blow in a Nordic biker war.
The Danish news agency Ritzau said it was feared that two people had died in what may have been a missile attack.
A hospital source told Reuters he understood two people had died and at least five had been injured.
Police could not immediately confirm that there had been any deaths but were expected to hold a news conference at 0400 GMT.
The most likely attacker was the rival Bandidos gang, which has waged a bloody turf war against the Hell's Angels for three years. Anti-tank missiles have been used by both sides.

But security officials have feared of late that a rising tide of public resentment against the gangs and their frequent gunfights and bomb raids in residential neighbourhoods could lead to some kind of vigilante action.

Copenhagen city council has been trying for weeks to force the Hell's Angels from their fortified clubhouse on Copenhagen's Titangade thoroughfare, near apartments and a hospital, and residents near another Hell's Angels property in the city have held street protests demanding their eviction.
A law allowing police to throw the gangs out of residential areas had its first parliamentary reading on Friday and the government has pledged that it will be law by the end of the coming week.

The gang war took on fresh intensity last March when attackers shot a Bandidos leader in the Finnish capital, Helsinki, and a Danish Bandido died in an ambush outside Copenhagen airport 10 days later.
The latest victim was a Danish Bandidos member who was shot in the head near the Norwegian city of Drammen in July.
